concepts.label: cbworkloadgen
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept anywhere in the registry or extraction layer. Generates random test data and read/write load against a Couchbase cluster or bucket.

concepts.label: cbstats
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the page's own worked example uses cbstats to look up a collection ID before it can be passed to cbworkloadgen's -c flag.

concepts.label: collection (Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the -c/--collection option scopes generated documents to a specific collection ID.

concepts.label: Port 8091
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the -n/--node option's default target address.

relations.subject: tool:cbworkloadgen
relations.evidence: To generate documents into the collection `my_collection` you first must find the collection ID. This can be done by using the command below: $ cbstats -u Administrator -p Password -b my-bucket 10.5.2.45:11210 collections | grep ":name:.*my_collection"

relations.subject: tool:cbworkloadgen
relations.evidence: The collection ID to perform the operations on. A collection with the given ID must exist. The ID is expected to be a number in hex format for example '0x16'.

relations.subject: tool:cbworkloadgen
relations.evidence: Target node address in the form `ip:port` or `hostname:port` for example `-n 127.0.0.1:8091`. If non provided it will default to `127.0.0.1:8091`.

notable_absence.finding: Like cbtransfer.md in this same batch, cbworkloadgen's -u/-p descriptions use the identical generic sentence 'If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error' with no role or privilege named - the third tool in the cbtools/ subdirectory in this batch to omit a specific RBAC citation, against cbrecovery being the one exception that names three roles. The wording match with cbtransfer's -u/-p options (verbatim, not just similar) suggests these two pages were copy-templated from each other and neither was subsequently filled in with real role names - a concrete, mechanically-detectable symptom of the lighter TW review this round is watching for in cli/.

cross_component_finding: cbworkloadgen's own worked example depends on tool:cbstats (a promoted concept) to resolve a collection name to a hex collection ID before cbworkloadgen can target it - a genuine, stated cross-tool dependency within the CLI suite, expressed nowhere else in the corpus for either tool. Neither page cross-references the other via a markdown link, though; the dependency is demonstrated in a worked example, not stated as a prerequisite in prose.
cross_product_finding: No Capella-specific content; cbworkloadgen targets a node:port address directly and is a load/test-data-generation tool for self-managed Server deployments.
